brief: Summer around the year 1500 in the Saint Lawrence valley: a warm sunny day with a light rain shower on one side, tall green corn, beans and squash growing in fields next to bark longhouses, a birchbark canoe gliding easily on a calm river. Clearly SUMMER: warm, green, growing. A few small original Iroquoian people working in the fields, respectful. No text.

Winter around the year 1500 in the Saint Lawrence valley: deep snow everywhere, a frozen river covered in ice, empty snowy fields where nothing grows, bark longhouses with smoke from the roof, one original Iroquoian person walking slowly with snowshoes through deep snow. Clearly WINTER: long, cold, hard to move around. No text.

Nomadic hunters long ago, before villages: a small group of original Indigenous people in fur clothing walking across a cold open land with their belongings on their backs, following a herd of caribou in the distance, a simple temporary shelter left behind. Clearly people who MOVE from place to place. Respectful and dignified. No text.
